lawyer:
Nawab Ali, Advocate-On-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
For the Respondents ------ Not Represented
parties:
Anwarullah and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur Court Building, Lakshmipur and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The petitioners as plaintiffs filed the Title Suit No.37 of 1993 in the Court of Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Lakshmipur for declaring their title to 5.71 acres of land described in Schedule 'Ka' to the plaint and for further declaration that .61 decimals of land described in Schedule 'Kha' out of the Schedule 'Ka' to the plaint is not vested and non-resident property against the respondent as defendants stating, inter-alia, that the plaintiffs claimed that 8 annas share of land appertaining to District Settlement Khatian No.351 of Bamni Mouza, under P.S. Roypur, belonged to Joy Gobindo Chowdhury who while possessing the same orally settled .75 decimals of land out of that land to Muslim Miah at a Jama of Tk. 6/-. Thereafter the said land was correctly recorded in the name of Muslim in District Settlement Khatian No.353. Thereafter Joy Gobinda Chowdhury settled 1.33 acres of land out of that land to one Joynal Abedin and the same has been recorded in the name of Joynal Abedin in the District Settlement Khatian No.354. Some Riyats, Ahmed Ali and others having defaulted in payment of rent to the landlord, Munir Hossain Haider and others who (land-lords)   then being plaintiffs filed rent suit being No.581 of 1922 in the 2nd Court of Munsif Lakshmipur and got the same decreed in respect of 5.75 acres of land in plot Nos. 304-308 appertaining to Khatian Nos. 351, 353, 354 and 355 which was then sold in auction in execution of the decree of the aforesaid rent suit and one Ambia Khatian auction purchased the same. The sale was confirmed on 12.9.1923 and the possession was delivered to the said auction purchaser on 8.12.1923. 

 5. The respondent-defendants contested the suit by filing separate written statements. The respondent Nos.1-3 as defendants-Government of Bangladesh in their written statement contended, inter-alia, that the Monoranjan Chandara, Shabitree Bala, Sharambala, Hira Lal and Makhon Lal were the original owners of the suit land and the same was recorded in their names in District settlement Khatian Nos. 351-353/354/355 and M.R.R. Khatian Nos. 359, 361, 362, 363 and 550 and that the said owners did never settle the suit land to any ,body and that the said owners while possessing the suit land left this country during Indo-Pak war of 1965 and thus, during the year 1967-68 the suit land was enlisted as Vested and Non-resident property. Thereafter defendant No. 20, Ahmed Ullah got settlement of .64 decimals of land from the Government and has been possessing the same within the knowledge of the plaintiffs and others. They have further contended that the plaintiffs alleged auction sale in respect of the suit land and all the papers in relation to that auction sale and subsequent thereto are all forged and concocted and created only with intent to grab the suit land being vested and non-resident property. Further they have contended that the plaintiffs have no right; title, interest and possession in the suit land and for the reasons mentioned above the suit are liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 6. The respondent Nos.6, 15-20, 29-36 as defendants filed written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to the Jaminder Nawab Sayd Hossain Haider Chowdhury, son of Syed Basharat Ali Chowdhury, Who never brought the Rent suit No. 581 of 1922 in the Second court of Munsiff, Lakshmipur and accordingly the suit land was never auction sold through Rent Execution Case No278 of 1923 and that one Ambia Khatun never auction purchased the suit land getting the sale Certificate and writ of Delivery of possession and that the plaintiffs   have created all their papers in relation to the aforesaid auction sale only with intent to grab the suit land and that they also never possessed the same. Further they have contended that one Mobarak Ali Chowdhury filed the suit being No. 151 of 1981 in the Court of subordinate Judge Lakshmipur against Monoranjan Chowdhury and others wherein the present plaintiffs, being defendant Nos. 17-21. contested the suit by filing written statement wherein they did not disclose the fact of their assertion as to the aforesaid suction purchase of the suit land through Rent suit No. 518 of 1922 and Rent Execution Case No. 278 of 1923. They have further contended that the M.R.R. Khatian being No. 351 in respect of the suit land was correctly prepared of which eight annas share belonged to Joy Gobindo Chowdhury and after him heirs Monoronjon Chowdhury and others vide registered kabala dated 17.11.1956, sold 67 decimals of land out of the suit land to the defendant No. 6 and his father, Bashirulah. Upon the death of 13ashrullah defendant No. 6 by amicable partition with his brothers and sisters got. 3312 decimals of land in his share in suit plot Nos. 305 and 306 and has been living by constructing house thereupon. Defendant No. 17 got his 47 decimals of land exchanged with defendant No. 20. Defendant Nos. 15-17 20/29-36 got land by purchase out of the suit land which arc in their possession. The plaintiffs have filed the suit on false allegations with intent to grab the suit land and hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. We have heard the learned Advocate-On-Record for the petitioners, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record. It appears that the High Court Division having considered the materials on record made concurrent findings   of the facts with the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge to the effect that some portion of Bainama is over written and some other portion of the Bainama appears to have been erased and signature of the Munshi appears to be illegible and over written which gave rise to concoction as to its veracity. The High Court Division rightly found that the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge having considered the evidence on record observed: "Ambia Khatun got possession of the suit land through the writ of delivery of possession marked as Ext.3 on the 29th November, 1923 and M.R.R. Khatians in question in respect of the suit land would have been prepared and published in the name of Ambia Khatun and her heirs and thus the Boinama marked Ext.2 and writ of delivery of possession marked Ext.3 appeared to have not been acted upon". The High Court Division also rightly found that the trial Court could not ascertain who were actually the decree holders and judgment debtors in the alleged Rent Suit No. 581 of 1922 and Rent Execution Case No.278 of 1923 and accordingly the trial court rightly held that the said Bainama and writ of delivery of possession were not genuine. The MRR Khatians prepared in 1960-61 would have been published in the names of the plaintiffs or the predecessors-in-interest. The High Court Division also found that the trial Court rightly held that there is no reliable witness to support the Boinama and writ of delivery of possession. The High Court Division has noticed that the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge found that Khatian No.350 filed by the contesting defendant shows that Nawbab Syed Hossain Haider Chowdhury's fathers name was late Syed Bosharat Ali Chowdhury. But in the disputed Boinama the fathers name was written as late Emdad Ali Chowdhury of different village which gave rise to concoction as to the veracity of the alleged Bainama and writ of delivery of possession. In Title Suit No.151 of 1981 the plaintiffs as defendant Nos.17-21 contested the suit by filing written statement but nowhere in their pleading they did disclose the fact that 1 their predecessor-in-interest got the suit land purchased by auction through Rent Suit No.581 of 1922 and Rent Execution Case No.278 of 1923 which has also been noticed by the High Court Division that C.S. owners of the land in Khatian Nos. 353, 354 and 355 were not made parties to the alleged Rent Suit No.581 of 1922 and Rent Execution Case No. 278 of 1923 and they were supposed to be in possession in their land but Ambia Khatun after her alleged auction purchase in respect of the land of those Khatian did not seek relief against those owners. The plaintiffs have also failed to show that their alleged predecessor-in-interest Ambia Khatun took over possession of the suit land appertaining to those Khatians by evicting the aforesaid Raiyati owners there from. Accordingly the High Court Division rightly observed that "It is very difficult to believe that the possession of the suit land was delivered to Abmia Khatun through auction sale vide the aforesaid Rent Execution Case No.278 of 1 1923". It appears that admittedly the suit lands belonged to one Joy Gobindo Chowdhury and after his death the suit property were inherited by his successors-in-interest who transferred their shares to the defendant No. 6 and their predecessors-in-interest by a registered kabala. The High Court Division on consideration of the material evidence on record rightly found that "all the findings of the Court below in coming to the decision disbelieving the plaintiffs case through the alleged Rent Suit and Rent Execution Case and considering the Bainama and the Writ of Delivery of Possession to be forged, interpolated   and created for the purpose of the suit and ultimately, dismissing the suit are all based on evidence on record and we find no reason to interfere with the same."
